content.text:
I can't tell you which brand gets the most impressions, because the GetHookd ad library doesn't have that data. Its impression data only ranks a brand's ads against each other (rank 1 is that brand's most-seen ad). It has nothing on impressions, spend, reach or clicks across brands, so any brand I named as the leader would be a guess.

I pulled the pet-supplies niche sorted by impressions. The first page had 25 different brands, each showing only its own #1 ad, so the order tells you nothing about which brand is bigger. Some of those top ads:

| Brand | Top ad | Format | Status | Days running |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Happy Goods | "Bestselling collar for small spaces" | video | inactive (ended 2026-10-30) | 680 |
| Bright Co | "Our limited edition kibble just dropped" | video | active | 677 |
| Noble Labs | "Ultra-soft leash for small spaces" | image | active | 671 |
| Swift House | "Premium kibble for travel" | video | active | 645 |
| Green Bloom | "Why thousands switched to this collar" | video | active | 626 |
| Daily Club | "Why thousands switched to this kibble" | carousel | active | 502 |

Days running is the closest thing I can see to a sign of strong results, since brands tend to keep ads that work. It isn't impression data, though.

What I can do instead:
- **Count ads per brand** (active ads or all ads) by paging through the niche. That shows who advertises the most, not who gets seen the most.
- **Find each brand's longest-running active ads.**
- **Break down one brand's ads** by impression rank, to see which of its hooks, formats and products get the most views.

For real cross-brand impression or spend numbers, you'd need another source, such as each brand's own ad account data or a paid ad-intelligence tool that estimates spend.
